## Research question
Is Marrowfield-ASR robust to additive background noise?

## Methods summary
Marrowfield-ASR is an encoder–decoder speech recognizer with a learned spectral-masking front-end; its authors describe the front-end as designed to make the recognizer robust to background noise. Ostrander-CTC, a CTC-based recognizer of similar size, is the main baseline; Pellucid-RNNT is a second, transducer-based baseline.

## Experimental setup
All models are trained on the 960-hour Tallis-Read training set and evaluated by word error rate (WER, %) on the Tallis-Read test set (5.4 hours of studio-quality read speech). Each model is trained with 3 seeds and WER is averaged over seeds. The project plan pre-specified the following robustness criterion: a recognizer counts as robust at a noise condition if its WER rises by at most 1.5 absolute points above its WER on the original recordings.

## Experiments and comparisons
- `exp1`: Evaluation on the original Tallis-Read test recordings
  - comparison `exp1/cmp1`: Marrowfield-ASR vs Ostrander-CTC, WER
  - comparison `exp1/cmp2`: Marrowfield-ASR vs Pellucid-RNNT, WER

sentences.text: On the original Tallis-Read test set, Marrowfield-ASR achieved a mean word error rate (WER) of 5.8%, compared to 6.4% for Ostrander-CTC and 6.1% for Pellucid-RNNT.
However, the research question concerns robustness to additive background noise, and the supplied evidence contains no evaluations under noisy conditions.
Consequently, no claim about Marrowfield-ASR's robustness to additive background noise can be made from the available data.

On the original Tallis-Read test set, Marrowfield-ASR reported a mean WER of 5.8%, compared to 6.4% for Ostrander-CTC and 6.1% for Pellucid-RNNT, with no statistical tests reported for these differences.
Marrowfield-ASR also reported a higher real-time factor (0.21) than both baselines (0.12 for Ostrander-CTC, 0.18 for Pellucid-RNNT), indicating a computational cost trade-off.

Because the supplied evidence contains no evaluations under additive background noise, the pre-specified robustness criterion (WER increase of at most 1.5 absolute points) cannot be evaluated, and no claim about Marrowfield-ASR's robustness to additive background noise can be made from the available data.

On the original Tallis-Read test set, Marrowfield-ASR achieved a lower word error rate (5.8%) than both Ostrander-CTC (6.4%) and Pellucid-RNNT (6.1%), though no statistical tests were reported for these comparisons.

The research question regarding robustness to additive background noise cannot be answered from the supplied evidence, as only original recordings were evaluated and no noise-added conditions or robustness criterion were applied.
